title: Pulmonary hamartoma: nodules of cartilage (disorganized mature tissue)
vignette: A 50-year-old man comes to the clinic for evaluation prior to a left total knee arthroplasty. Medical history is significant for osteoarthritis. The patient does not smoke. Preoperative chest x-ray demonstrates a 1.5-cm, round lesion in the periphery of the right upper lobe of the lung. Further imaging studies are suggestive of a pulmonary hamartoma. If a transthoracic biopsy were performed, which of the following microscopic features would be most consistent with this diagnosis?

clues.note: A nonsmoker with an incidental peripheral nodule lowers the probability of bronchogenic carcinoma and fits a benign lesion like hamartoma.
A small (<3 cm), round, well-circumscribed PERIPHERAL 'coin lesion' is the typical appearance of a pulmonary hamartoma.
Hamartomas are composed of tissues native to the organ but disorganized - in the lung, nodules of mature cartilage and fat with entrapped respiratory epithelium.

whatMatters: A small, round, well-circumscribed PERIPHERAL coin lesion in a nonsmoker suggestive of pulmonary hamartoma. Hamartomas are benign lesions of DISORGANIZED MATURE tissue native to the organ - in the lung, NODULES OF CARTILAGE (and fat) with clefts lined by entrapped respiratory epithelium. Answer D.
strategy: Recall the hamartoma definition: normal/mature tissue types native to the organ, arranged abnormally (benign, slow-growing). In the lung that means cartilage nodules ± fat + respiratory epithelium. Reject the malignant histologies: atypical alveolar-lining cells (adenocarcinoma in situ), neuroendocrine markers (small cell/carcinoid), keratin pearls/invasive nests (squamous cell carcinoma), and sheets of large pleomorphic cells (large cell carcinoma).

options.text: Atypical cells lining alveoli without invasion
Invasive nests with keratin pearl formation

eliminations.label: Atypical cells lining alveoli without invasion - adenocarcinoma in situ
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: atypical cells growing along alveolar septa (lepidic pattern) without invasion = adenocarcinoma in situ. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is a malignant (or premalignant) glandular lesion, not a benign hamartoma. ✅ Correct if: a peripheral adenocarcinoma in situ (lepidic growth).

eliminations.label: Neuroendocrine markers - small cell/carcinoid
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: synaptophysin/chromogranin expression = neuroendocrine tumors (small cell carcinoma, carcinoid). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: these are malignant/neuroendocrine (small cell is central and smoking-related), not a hamartoma. ✅ Correct if: small cell carcinoma or carcinoid tumor.

eliminations.label: Invasive nests + keratin pearls - squamous cell carcinoma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: invasive nests of keratinizing cells with keratin pearls = squamous cell carcinoma. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is a malignant, usually central, smoking-related tumor, not a benign cartilaginous nodule. ✅ Correct if: central squamous cell carcinoma.

eliminations.label: Sheets of large pleomorphic cells - large cell carcinoma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sheets of large, undifferentiated pleomorphic cells = large cell carcinoma (diagnosis of exclusion). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is an aggressive malignancy, not a hamartoma. ✅ Correct if: an enlarging necrotic peripheral mass that is large cell carcinoma.

reasoning: Small, round, well-circumscribed peripheral coin lesion in a nonsmoker = likely benign pulmonary hamartoma
Hamartomas are disorganized MATURE tissues native to the organ
In the lung: nodules of cartilage (and fat) with entrapped respiratory epithelium
-> nodules of cartilaginous tissue; answer D
mechanism: A hamartoma is a benign lesion composed of tissue types NATIVE to the organ but arranged in a disorganized fashion. Pulmonary hamartomas are common, usually asymptomatic, incidentally discovered lung lesions in middle-aged adults; radiographically they are typically solitary, small (<3 cm), round, well-circumscribed peripheral 'coin lesions' that grow slowly and may show a 'popcorn' pattern of calcification. Microscopically they show NODULES of mature CARTILAGE (chondroid tissue), often with fat and fibrous tissue, and clefts lined by entrapped respiratory (bronchial) epithelium. Although historically called malformations, many are now considered benign neoplasms (clonal chromosomal abnormalities). Their benign, mature-tissue histology contrasts with the malignant options, which describe primary lung cancers: adenocarcinoma in situ (atypical lepidic cells), small cell/carcinoid (neuroendocrine markers), squamous cell carcinoma (keratin pearls/invasive nests), and large cell carcinoma (sheets of large pleomorphic cells).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Path/Pulm > pulmonary hamartoma: benign, peripheral coin lesion, popcorn calcification; disorganized mature cartilage + fat + entrapped respiratory epithelium; contrast primary lung cancers.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Hamartoma = mature native tissue arranged abnormally -> cartilage nodules (benign).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on hamartoma, coin lesion, chondroid/cartilage, lepidic growth, or keratin pearls? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Atypical alveolar cells = adenocarcinoma in situ; neuroendocrine markers = small cell/carcinoid; keratin pearls = squamous cell; pleomorphic sheets = large cell.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: pulmonary hamartoma = benign cartilage (+ fat) nodule with respiratory epithelium; peripheral coin lesion, popcorn calcification.

memoryHook: A hamartoma is the organ's own tissue thrown together sloppily - in the lung, a benign popcorn-calcified coin lesion made of cartilage nodules, not cancer.
